rationale: Run the probe the snapshot child question asks for. The new case uses the snapshot-capable entry type, repeats the three reconnection rounds that witness the drift, and then requests snapshot(Some(8), false) on the leader - an index strictly inside the drifted decided index but above the six indices of content - with the call wrapped so a panic is reported, and emits the call outcome, the compacted index, the leader's accepted and decided indexes and how many entry ids the snapshot reachable at index 0 holds. The comparisons require the six-index baseline before the call, that the call is accepted, that the compacted index does not pass the six indices of content, that the produced snapshot holds the five decided entries, and that every replica still reports six indices afterwards; the source prediction is that the request is accepted and the snapshot is built from an empty range, so the compacted index passes the content and the snapshot holds none of the entries.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a drift-then-snapshot case over the snapshot-capable entry type: three reconnection rounds, then snapshot(Some(8), false) on the leader inside the drifted decided index, reporting the call outcome, the compacted index and the number of entries the produced snapshot holds.

scope.description: Nine cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case uses the snapshot-capable entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true with a snapshot that records the entry ids), drifts the recorded and decided indexes with three reconnection rounds, then calls snapshot(Some(8), false) on the leader wrapped in catch_unwind and reports the outcome, the compacted index, the leader's accepted and decided indexes, and how many entry ids the snapshot reachable at index 0 holds.
assumptions: SnapEntry/SnapState are the snapshot-capable entry type already used by the snap case; SnapState::create records the entry ids of the slice it is given, so an empty range yields a snapshot with no ids.
Three reconnection rounds of nodes 1 and 2 reproduce the drift (accepted and decided indexes above the six indices of content) as witnessed for the NoSnapshot entry type.

The snapshot index 8 is strictly below the drifted decided index (9) and above the six indices of content, so try_snapshot's equal case does not apply; the call is wrapped so a panic is reported as a field.
excluded: No trim is called in this case, and no other case is changed.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: The new case builds three OmniPaxos<SnapEntry, MemoryStorage<SnapEntry>> instances with the validated three-node config, makes node 3 leader with try_become_leader(), appends SnapEntry{id: 0..4} and drains the queue, proposes and decides a StopSign with reconfigure() and drains, then performs three rounds of node1.reconnected(3)+node2.reconnected(3) with the queue drained each round. It samples all nodes as DRSNAP_BEFORE, calls c.node(3).snapshot(Some(8), false) inside catch_unwind and emits DRSNAP_SNAP with snap_outcome (ok/err/panic), compacted_idx, accepted_idx, decided_idx and snap_ids (the number of entry ids in the snapshot reachable at index 0, or -1 if index 0 is not snapshotted), then samples all nodes as DRSNAP_AFTER.

comparisons.description: Before the snapshot the snapshot-capable cluster's replicas report the six indices they hold.
A snapshot request inside the drifted decided index is accepted.
A snapshot does not compact past the entries the configuration holds: the compacted index stays at the six indices of content.
The snapshot holds the five decided entries the log contained.
After the snapshot every replica still reports the six indices it holds.

semantic_changes: Adds the drift-then-snapshot case over the snapshot-capable entry type; every previously generated case is unchanged apart from sharing one execution.
